display.title: Tanya Shiur 32: End of Chapter 14, Loving Hashem and Rejecting Evil
display.summary_short: A Yiddish shiur finishing Tanya chapter 14: why the beinoni cannot fully hate evil, and how daily reflection and joy bring him closer. The file then repeats the next shiur's opening.
display.summary_long: Shiur 32 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series completes chapter 14. True hatred of evil comes only with love of Hashem that is a delight, the level of a tzaddik, a taste of the World to Come; the Rambam compares explaining that delight to describing colors to a blind man. The fifty gates of understanding, the forty-nine days of the Omer, Moshe Rabbeinu on Har Nevo and the blessing Refa'einu show that the highest level comes as a gift. This answers the Alter Rebbe's question from chapter 1 about Iyov's words 'You created tzaddikim' and the double oath. 'There is no good but Torah': the Rebbe's lullaby 'Torah is the best merchandise', start learning now, and draw others close in a positive way. A small turn off the road becomes a great distance. The beinoni should set a daily time to reflect on the lowliness of worldly pleasures and the greatness of Hashem, chase away sadness with joy, and leap, and Hashem helps; he may even receive a spark of a tzaddik's soul. After the closing, the recording repeats the opening of the next week's shiur and stops in the middle of a Baal Shem Tov story.
display.lesson: Do everything you can to love Hashem and reject evil, and Hashem will give the rest as a gift.
